name: Jewish secularism
summary: Jewish secularism holds that Jews are a people with a shared history and culture rather than a community of faith, and that Jewish life can be lived without God or religious law. Today it is carried by Humanistic Judaism and secular Jewish federations in the diaspora and by the large secular (hiloni) public in Israel. Its politics centre on separating religion from the state, personal autonomy (reproductive choice, LGBT equality, aid in dying, free choice of marriage partner), gender equality and democracy over religious authority, together with support for Israel as the creation of secular Zionism.
scope: The living ideology: Humanistic Judaism (Sherwin Wine, the Society for Humanistic Judaism and its Jews for a Secular Democracy initiative, the International Institute and the International Federation of Secular Humanistic Jews and their rabbis' and leaders' resolutions), the Congress of Secular Jewish Organizations, and Israeli secularism as shown by the hiloni public and Hiddush-style religious-freedom positions (Liebman and Yadgar's 'secular Judaists'). The 19th-century and interwar roots (Ahad Ha'am, Dubnow, the Bund, Yiddishism) are background only, so their diaspora-autonomy and socialist programmes are not counted as current positions. Where diaspora humanists and Israeli secularists differ (for example on security and the Law of Return), or where the movement takes no economic line, answers are neutral or low. Anti-Zionist secular universalists and religious movements (Reform, Reconstructionist, Orthodox) are excluded.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Inferred from the movement's commitment to justice and to meeting human needs; diaspora humanists lean progressive while Israeli secularists already live with a universal system, but no resolution addresses it.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: No secular Jewish body takes an economic line, and Israeli hilonim mostly place themselves in the political centre, so this is left neutral.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Secular Jews span Meretz's left to the market-liberal Shinui and Yesh Atid electorate, so the movement has no view on markets versus the state.

public-ownership.rationale: Economic ownership lies outside what secular Jewish organisations take positions on, and their Israeli base runs from centre-left to centre-right.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: No secular Jewish platform deals with tax levels; the Israeli secular public is mostly centrist, so the answer stays neutral.

unions-good.rationale: Unions mattered to the historical Bundist roots, but today's humanistic and Israeli secular bodies say nothing about labour, so this is left neutral.

property-fundamental.rationale: The movement has no doctrine on property rights; its concerns are religion, identity and civil liberties.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Corporate regulation is outside the religion-and-identity agenda of secular Jewish groups, and their adherents differ on economics.

cut-welfare.rationale: Inferred from the stress on justice and on compassion; Hiddush's grievance is welfare for yeshiva students who do not work, not welfare as such.

worker-ownership.rationale: Cooperative ownership belonged to the old socialist and kibbutz roots, not to the contemporary movement's positions.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Inferred from the 1986 commitment that individual privacy and moral autonomy must be guaranteed.

legalize-drugs.rationale: The Society for Humanistic Judaism joined a 2021 resolution calling for full legalisation of cannabis for medical and recreational use, consistent with its stress on personal autonomy.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Equal rights and tolerance point one way and the defence of free inquiry the other; no secular Jewish body has taken a position.

strong-leader.rationale: Democracy is one of the universal standards the federation's principles adopt, and secular Israelis are the group most committed to democratic procedure over any higher authority.

state-harmful.rationale: The movement looks to the state to guarantee rights, separation of religion and equal civil status, which presupposes a state.

limit-guns.rationale: No secular Jewish statement addresses gun ownership; it is left neutral.

empower-police-military.rationale: Israeli secularists back the army (and want Haredim drafted into it) while diaspora humanists are more dovish, so there is no common view.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: The rabbis' sexual-ethics work affirms adult autonomy, but no resolution addresses commercial sex.

decide-locally.rationale: The movement is about religion and identity, not levels of government; nothing points either way.

rehabilitation.rationale: Inferred from the humanist faith in human capacity and dignity; no statement addresses prisons.

traditional-family.rationale: Humanistic Judaism affirms same-sex couples, intermarriage and free choice of partners, rejecting a single traditional family model as normative.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: The 2004 leadership resolution calls for full legal equality for LGBT people including marriage, and the SHJ backed legal recognition of same-sex marriage and divorce the same year.

abortion-legal.rationale: A 1996 SHJ statement says a woman has the moral and continuing legal right to decide whether to end a pregnancy, and Jews for a Secular Democracy campaigns for abortion access.

more-religion-public.rationale: Pew finds 88% of Israeli hilonim want religion kept separate from government policy, and the 1986 federation commitments warn against resurgent fundamentalism.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Inferred from the commitment to equal rights regardless of race and to freedom and equality for all; no specific programme is stated.

gender-social-construct.rationale: The rabbis affirm diverse gender identities but take no theoretical position on how gender arises.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Jewish languages, literature, music and holidays are one of the federation's ten commitments, and Israel's secular Judaists work to strengthen Jewish culture; but it is reinterpreted culture, not tradition preserved as it was.

gradual-change.rationale: The movement values creative renewal of tradition but works through democratic institutions; it is neither for nor against gradualism as such.

reduce-immigration.rationale: The humanistic rabbis opposed the 2017 travel ban and cite 'we were strangers'; in Israel, secularists favour Jewish immigration under the Law of Return. Reducing immigration is opposed, though no general policy is stated.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Diaspora humanists endorse peace and international standards, while Israeli secularists share Israel's distrust of the UN; no shared view.

free-trade.rationale: Trade policy falls outside secular Jewish platforms.

nation-first.rationale: Inferred from the commitment to learn from other cultures and adopt universal standards of tolerance and peace.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: No secular Jewish body has taken a view on military intervention abroad.

open-borders.rationale: The movement backs Israel as a Jewish state with a Law of Return, which assumes controlled borders; diaspora humanists are more open, so this is weak.

limit-growth.rationale: Environmental economics is outside the movement's stated positions.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Inferred from the stress on reason and science as guides to action; no climate resolution was found.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Humanists trust reason and human power to solve problems, but nothing commits them to technological optimism specifically.

revolution-justified.rationale: The revolutionary socialism of the Bundist roots has no successor in today's democratic, reformist movement; it is left neutral.

experts-over-public.rationale: Reason and evidence are prized, but democracy is equally affirmed; no view on expert rule.

central-planning.rationale: Secular Israelis vote mainly for centrist and market-friendly parties; inferred weak disagreement.

socialized-markets.rationale: No economic doctrine in the contemporary movement.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Nothing in the movement is anti-market in this sense; its Israeli base is centrist, so mild disagreement is inferred.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Secular Jewish bodies take no position on this; mild disagreement is inferred from the mainstream, democratic politics of their adherents.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: No position on corporatist wage setting.

one-party-rule.rationale: The 1986 commitments call for a secular humanistic democracy in Israel and worldwide, and the principles name democracy and pluralism as standards; rule by one ideological party contradicts both.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Inferred from the commitment to equality and democracy; no statement on constitutional monarchy.

democracy-best.rationale: Pew reports that 89% of Israeli hilonim would give democratic principles priority over Jewish law if the two conflict, and the federation's principles adopt democracy as a universal standard.

direct-votes.rationale: No view on direct versus representative democracy.

workers-councils.rationale: The movement works within parliamentary democracy; council power has no place in it today.

natural-rulers.rationale: The commitments to equal rights for every person and to equality of all people rule out a natural ruling class.

political-violence-never.rationale: Liebman and Yadgar note that secular study circles stress eschewing violence, yet most secularists accept Israel's right to defend itself by force; the literal 'never' is not taken up.

war-builds-character.rationale: Inferred from the commitment to the pursuit of peace.

separate-church-state.rationale: The 1986 federation commitments state that religion and state must be separate, and the SHJ's Jews for a Secular Democracy initiative exists to keep religion out of government.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Pew finds 90% of hilonim oppose making Jewish law the state law for Jews, and the federation rejects reliance on supernatural authority.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Inferred: the movement wants a state that guarantees equal civil status and shares military service, not private provision.

military-superiority.rationale: Israeli secularists support a strong army while diaspora humanists stress peace; no common position.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Most Israeli secularists back a Jewish state and 69% say Jews deserve preferential treatment, while secular universalists and many diaspora humanists want no distinction between Jews and Arabs; strands are split.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Humanistic Judaism reads history as the result of human decisions and actions rather than any single driving force; Marxist history belongs to the Bundist past.

equal-outcomes.rationale: No position on equality of outcome.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Neither the humanistic movement nor Israeli secular groups take a position on this, and nothing in their principles decides it, so it is left neutral.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Neither the humanistic movement nor Israeli secular groups take a position on this, and nothing in their principles decides it, so it is left neutral.

civilizational-union.rationale: Inferred from opposition to politics organised by religion.

self-interest-moral.rationale: The principles praise personal dignity and self-mastery alongside responsibility for justice; neither endorses self-interest as moral in itself.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Inferred from the stress on individual moral autonomy and being master of one's own life.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Celebrating the seasons of nature is part of the movement, but no ethical claim about nature's value is made.

limit-population.rationale: Neither the humanistic movement nor Israeli secular groups take a position on this, and nothing in their principles decides it, so it is left neutral.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Inferred from the humanist confidence in reason and human achievement.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Neither the humanistic movement nor Israeli secular groups take a position on this, and nothing in their principles decides it, so it is left neutral.

human-enhancement.rationale: Autonomy would favour it, but no statement addresses enhancement.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Inferred from the commitment to democratic self-government.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Privacy is affirmed in 1986, but encryption has not been addressed.

restore-past-order.rationale: The principles hold that the creativity of the present may carry equal or greater authority than the past, and Humanistic Judaism treats Judaism as a changing human creation.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Inferred from the reliance on reason and evidence and the acceptance of uncertainty.

direct-action.rationale: Secular Jewish groups work through litigation, advocacy and elections (Hiddush's court cases, JFASD lobbying).

means-match-ends.rationale: Neither the humanistic movement nor Israeli secular groups take a position on this, and nothing in their principles decides it, so it is left neutral.

return-to-foraging.rationale: The movement celebrates human knowledge and power to shape the world; a return to foraging runs against its core humanism.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Secular Jewish bodies take no position on this; mild disagreement is inferred from the mainstream, democratic politics of their adherents.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Neither the humanistic movement nor Israeli secular groups take a position on this, and nothing in their principles decides it, so it is left neutral.

production-for-use.rationale: Neither the humanistic movement nor Israeli secular groups take a position on this, and nothing in their principles decides it, so it is left neutral.

profit-exploitation.rationale: No position; the Marxist strand of the roots is not carried on.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: A class dictatorship contradicts the commitments to democracy, pluralism and equal rights for all.

collective-farming.rationale: Kibbutz collectivism is part of secular Zionist history, but no current position is taken.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Neither the humanistic movement nor Israeli secular groups take a position on this, and nothing in their principles decides it, so it is left neutral.

taxation-theft.rationale: Inferred: the movement expects the state to fund public goods fairly and equitably.

harm-principle.rationale: The commitments say individual privacy and moral autonomy must be guaranteed, and JFASD opposes laws that impose religious belief on personal choices.

individual-rights-only.rationale: The movement stresses individual autonomy yet also defends the collective rights of the Jewish people and equality for streams of Judaism; strands are split.

conscription.rationale: Hiddush wants military or civil service shared equally including by yeshiva students, and 90% of hilonim favour drafting Haredi men, which presupposes conscription.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Inferred from the weight placed on democratic participation.

state-as-business.rationale: Secular Jewish bodies take no position on this; mild disagreement is inferred from the mainstream, democratic politics of their adherents.

positive-liberty.rationale: Inferred from the stress on dignity and Hiddush's concern that the poor, elderly and disabled lack weekend transport.

media-academia-power.rationale: The SHJ defended academic freedom in 2014; it does not see universities as an illegitimate power.

hereditarian-race.rationale: The commitment to equal rights regardless of race and the movement's rationalist universalism reject racial hierarchy.

organic-representation.rationale: Inferred from the commitment to individual-based democracy.

total-state.rationale: The 1986 commitments demand that individual privacy and moral autonomy be guaranteed and that religion and state be separate, the opposite of a state directing every area of life.

national-rebirth.rationale: Israeli secular Judaists speak of a Jewish cultural renaissance, but not of a radical national rebirth from decadence.

territorial-expansion.rationale: The SHJ endorsed a two-state solution in 2002, and a plurality of hilonim say settlements hurt Israel's security.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Personal fealty is incompatible with the democratic and egalitarian standards the movement adopts.

bound-labor.rationale: Bound labour contradicts the commitment that every person is entitled to life, dignity and freedom.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Inferred from the federation's confidence that reason can find truth about the world.

universal-morality.rationale: The principles adopt universal standards of tolerance, democracy and equality, and secular study circles present these as universal humanist values.

single-common-good.rationale: Pluralism is prized, which leans against a single common good, but nothing explicit.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: The SHJ and IISHJ support Zionism and the State of Israel and its right to defend itself, and the federation calls Israel the major achievement of the secular Zionist movement; anti-Zionist secular universalists are a minority.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: 98% of Israeli hilonim say it is the birthright of Jews to make aliyah, and the humanistic movement supports Israel; but its view of a Jew as anyone who chooses to identify complicates descent-based return.

revive-national-language.rationale: Hebrew revival was historic secular Zionism; today the movement values Jewish languages including Yiddish without a revival programme.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Neither the humanistic movement nor Israeli secular groups take a position on this, and nothing in their principles decides it, so it is left neutral.

school-vouchers.rationale: Jews for a Secular Democracy defends secular public education, and Hiddush objects to public money for schools that skip the core curriculum.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Neither the humanistic movement nor Israeli secular groups take a position on this, and nothing in their principles decides it, so it is left neutral.

economic-freedom.rationale: Neither the humanistic movement nor Israeli secular groups take a position on this, and nothing in their principles decides it, so it is left neutral.

rule-by-example.rationale: Inferred from the preference for laws and rights over personal authority.

national-self-determination.rationale: Humanistic Zionism rests on Jews being a people rather than only a religion, and the SHJ's two-state position extends self-determination to Palestinians.

force-without-un.rationale: Neither the humanistic movement nor Israeli secular groups take a position on this, and nothing in their principles decides it, so it is left neutral.

reason-over-faith.rationale: The principles commit members to seek truth through reason, and the 1986 commitments affirm reason and a natural universe that needs no supernatural intervention.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Inferred from the rabbis' compassion for immigrants and refugees.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Hiddush wants yeshiva students to join the workforce, but no general position on workfare.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: The movement builds on studying Jewish history, literature and texts; destroying inherited culture opposes its programme of reinterpretation.

dominated-front.rationale: Anti-Western blocs are foreign to the movement's concerns; Israeli secularists are Western-aligned and diaspora humanists take no view, so it is left neutral.

workers-nation.rationale: Neither the humanistic movement nor Israeli secular groups take a position on this, and nothing in their principles decides it, so it is left neutral.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: The principles adopt equality of status for men and women, and Hiddush says women must not be disadvantaged by religious rules in buses, personal status or public places.

ban-interest.rationale: Inferred: religious bans on interest are what the movement rejects as law.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: The 1986 commitments require equal rights regardless of race, sex, creed or ethnic origin.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Neither the humanistic movement nor Israeli secular groups take a position on this, and nothing in their principles decides it, so it is left neutral.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Neither the humanistic movement nor Israeli secular groups take a position on this, and nothing in their principles decides it, so it is left neutral.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Inferred from pluralism and openness to other cultures; the movement itself is a minority culture keeping its identity.

elite-replacement.rationale: The movement's rationalism and its rabbis' defence of refugees reject the replacement conspiracy theory.

proportional-representation.rationale: Israel's secular parties (Meretz, Shinui) live within proportional representation; inferred mild support.

national-mission.rationale: Inferred from openness and learning from other cultures.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: The SHJ condemned gender discrimination in all its forms in 2013 and Hiddush names religious disadvantage to women; a structural theory is not stated.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Secular anger targets the religious parties, not elites in general.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Reproductive autonomy and the right of every person to life and dignity rule this out.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Inferred from the commitment to life, dignity and the rule of law.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Hiddush expects the state to provide education, transport and fair allocation; inferred mild disagreement.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: The 1991 intermarriage resolution affirms the right to choose one's partner whatever their background, and the movement has celebrated intercultural marriage for decades.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: The 1986 commitments state that every person is entitled to life, dignity and freedom and to equal rights regardless of race, sex, creed or ethnicity.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Neither the humanistic movement nor Israeli secular groups take a position on this, and nothing in their principles decides it, so it is left neutral.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: The movement supports Zionism and calls Israel a major achievement of the Jewish people, rejecting a colonial label; anti-Zionist secularists are a minority.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Hiddush wants civil marriage and divorce open to all instead of religious courts ruling on personal status, a goal backed by large secular majorities.

restrict-conversion.rationale: The movement welcomes anyone who identifies with the Jewish people without required conversion, and Hiddush opposes revoking lenient conversions.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Inferred: a religious ban imposed by law runs against separation of religion and state.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: JFASD defends secular public education and opposes religious instruction imposed by government, in line with the separation commitment.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: No position; socialist-state doctrine is foreign to the movement.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Humanistic Judaism locates authority in human beings rather than God, and secular Israelis put democracy above religious law.

trade-surplus.rationale: Neither the humanistic movement nor Israeli secular groups take a position on this, and nothing in their principles decides it, so it is left neutral.

population-transfer.rationale: Equal rights point against it and 58% of hilonim reject expelling Arabs, but 36% agree, so this is held at mild disagreement.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Neither the humanistic movement nor Israeli secular groups take a position on this, and nothing in their principles decides it, so it is left neutral.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Neither the humanistic movement nor Israeli secular groups take a position on this, and nothing in their principles decides it, so it is left neutral.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Inferred from the call for freedom from religious coercion even where it is rarely enforced.

separated-powers.rationale: Hiddush relies on Israel's Supreme Court to check the rabbinate and coalition; inferred support.

vanguard-party.rationale: Vanguard rule contradicts the pluralism and democracy the movement takes as standards.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Justice is a core value, but no priority-to-the-poor principle is stated.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Neither the humanistic movement nor Israeli secular groups take a position on this, and nothing in their principles decides it, so it is left neutral.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Neither the humanistic movement nor Israeli secular groups take a position on this, and nothing in their principles decides it, so it is left neutral.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Neither the humanistic movement nor Israeli secular groups take a position on this, and nothing in their principles decides it, so it is left neutral.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: The federation's principles say diversity in Jewish life is a strength, not a weakness, and commit to pluralism.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Neither the humanistic movement nor Israeli secular groups take a position on this, and nothing in their principles decides it, so it is left neutral.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Inferred from the guarantee of privacy, autonomy and rights.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Neither the humanistic movement nor Israeli secular groups take a position on this, and nothing in their principles decides it, so it is left neutral.

party-controls-media.rationale: Pluralism, democracy and the SHJ's defence of academic freedom oppose party control of information.

party-commands-army.rationale: Inferred from the movement's democratic commitments.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Inferred from the rabbis' welcome to immigrants and the support for immediate citizenship under the Law of Return.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Neither the humanistic movement nor Israeli secular groups take a position on this, and nothing in their principles decides it, so it is left neutral.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Neither the humanistic movement nor Israeli secular groups take a position on this, and nothing in their principles decides it, so it is left neutral.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Neither the humanistic movement nor Israeli secular groups take a position on this, and nothing in their principles decides it, so it is left neutral.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Neither the humanistic movement nor Israeli secular groups take a position on this, and nothing in their principles decides it, so it is left neutral.

church-by-bishops.rationale: The movement's congregations govern themselves; inferred mild disagreement with episcopal rule.

clerical-rule.rationale: 90% of hilonim oppose making halakha state law and 89% put democracy above it, and the federation rejects supernatural authority.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: The SHJ affirmed Israel's right to defend its citizens; inferred disagreement.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Creativity, reason and freedom from religious morality imposed by law are central commitments.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Neither the humanistic movement nor Israeli secular groups take a position on this, and nothing in their principles decides it, so it is left neutral.

recall-officials.rationale: Neither the humanistic movement nor Israeli secular groups take a position on this, and nothing in their principles decides it, so it is left neutral.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Neither the humanistic movement nor Israeli secular groups take a position on this, and nothing in their principles decides it, so it is left neutral.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Secular Jewish bodies take no position on this; mild disagreement is inferred from the mainstream, democratic politics of their adherents.

people-in-arms.rationale: Hiddush wants a shared draft, but a citizen army replacing a professional one is not discussed.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: No position; agrarian romanticism belonged to early secular Zionism.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Neither the humanistic movement nor Israeli secular groups take a position on this, and nothing in their principles decides it, so it is left neutral.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Inferred from the value placed on study and learning.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: The movement learns from all cultures but judges them by universal standards of tolerance and equality; no relativist view.

death-penalty.rationale: Inferred from the commitment to every person's right to life; Israel has no regular death penalty.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Jews for a Secular Democracy supports comprehensive, evidence-based sex education in schools.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: The movement grounds knowledge in reason and science and wants standardised secular subjects in schools.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Inferred from adult moral autonomy and privacy.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Israeli secularists back the Law of Return, while diaspora humanists live in birthright-citizenship countries; no clear view.

minority-language-support.rationale: Inferred from the commitment to Jewish languages and pluralism.

religious-exemptions.rationale: The SHJ opposed conscience clauses in 2012, JFASD opposes religious exemptions that allow discrimination, and Hiddush wants yeshiva students to serve.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Inferred from the commitment to personal dignity and creativity.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Neither the humanistic movement nor Israeli secular groups take a position on this, and nothing in their principles decides it, so it is left neutral.

notes: Re-scoped 2026-10-21 from an interwar-peak profile (Bund, Dubnow, Ahad Ha'am) to the living ideology. Israeli secularists and diaspora humanists agree on religion and state and personal autonomy but differ in emphasis on security, settlements and the Law of Return; about a third of hilonim agree Arabs should be expelled, against the movement's equal-rights commitments, so those questions are low. The movement has no economic programme, so economic statements are mostly neutral. Note: Hiddush backs freedom of and from religion but not necessarily complete separation; the federation and JFASD state separation outright.
